why_the_standard_update_breaks_this_came: the online update (Web UI GitHub update, sysupgrade -k -r without --archive, --url, --channel, --build, auto-update) takes the -split.tgz package when it exists and writes its firmware.bin from 0x070000 in one piece

firmware.bin of the installed version is 7012352 bytes and ends at 0x720000 only because its kernel rounds up to exactly the 0x1d0000 slot; nightly 4cc6476 is 7077888 bytes and ends at 0x730000, so its squashfs runs past the rootfs slot into rootfs_data
the plain package of nightly 4cc6476 has a 5124096-byte rootfs, 12288 bytes more than the 5111808-byte rootfs slot (its 1864788-byte kernel fits)
without -z the updater first replaces itself with OpenIPC master's
-u rewrites U-Boot; -f and --force_* turn off the updater's own checks; --no_ramfs flashes the running system

layers.guard: passes on only --kernel/--rootfs images of this SoC that fit their slots and are whole, --archive with a plain package whose images fit (never firmware.bin, no extra files), -k -r only with --archive, -n -x -s -z --web --insecure, and read-only -h --help --history --list-builds; always adds -z; refuses every write when /rom's updater is not a version that was read (1.0.84); refusals go to logger -t sysupgrade-guard
layers.env_upgrade: the updater uses it only when no --url, --channel or --build is given; .invalid never resolves, so the Web UI update button, sysupgrade -k -r and auto-update fetch nothing even without the guard; --channel and --build are not covered
layers.factory_reset: sysupgrade -n, firstboot and the Web UI reset wipe the overlay and the guard with it; the env stays; run easy/post_setup.py again after the owner's first login
